pyq_focus: Unit 8 mein NET sabse zyada 'critic - book - term' match poochta hai: Aristotle - Poetics - catharsis, Longinus - On the Sublime, Sidney - An Apology for Poetry.
Indian aesthetics har saal aata hai: Bharata ka Natyashastra aur rasa sutra, Anandavardhana ka Dhvanyaloka, Kuntaka ka vakrokti, Kshemendra ka auchitya, Vamana ka riti.
Eliot ke terms bahut pakke karo: objective correlative, dissociation of sensibility, impersonality, tradition - aur kaun sa term kis essay ka hai.
Romantic criticism: Wordsworth ka Preface (1800/1802) definition of poetry, Coleridge ki Biographia Literaria (1817) - fancy vs imagination, willing suspension of disbelief.
Arnold (touchstone method, criticism of life, 'disinterestedness'), Pater (gem-like flame), Johnson (Preface to Shakespeare, Lives of the Poets) - quotes ke through poochte hain.

New Criticism: Brooks (Well Wrought Urn, heresy of paraphrase), Wimsatt-Beardsley (intentional aur affective fallacy), Ransom (The New Criticism 1941), Richards (Practical Criticism 1929, four kinds of meaning), Empson (Seven Types of Ambiguity 1930).
Frye ka Anatomy of Criticism (1957) - four mythoi aur seasons; Russian Formalism - Shklovsky ka defamiliarization, fabula-syuzhet, Jakobson ka literariness.

Chronology questions ke liye saal yaad karo: Apology 1595, Essay of Dramatic Poesy 1668, Essay on Criticism 1711, Preface to Shakespeare 1765, Biographia 1817, Defence 1821 (pub. 1840), Tradition 1919, Practical Criticism 1929, Anatomy 1957.
Tayyari: har critic ka ek card banao - book + saal + 2 terms + 1 famous quote; Assertion-Reason ke liye term ka matlab bhi samjho, sirf naam nahi.

easy.title: Plato (c. 428-348 BCE): Poetry as Imitation
easy.story: Plato kehte the asli cheez 'Idea' hai, jo upar ek perfect duniya mein hai. Carpenter jo kursi banata hai woh Idea ki copy hai. Painter ya poet us kursi ki tasveer banata hai, toh woh copy ki copy hai - 'twice removed from truth'. Isliye Plato ne Republic (Book III aur X) mein poets ko apne ideal state se nikal diya. Unhe lagta tha poetry emotions bhadkati hai aur log bigad jaate hain. Ion mein unhone kaha poet 'divine madness' mein likhta hai, gyaan se nahi.
easy.trick: Plato = 'Photocopy ki Photocopy' - Idea > kursi > tasveer; Republic X = poets ko 'eXit'.

easy.title: Aristotle (384-322 BCE): Poetics
easy.story: Aristotle Plato ke student the, par unhone guru se ulta kaha: imitation (mimesis) toh insaan ki natural aadat hai aur usse hum seekhte hain. Poetics mein tragedy ki definition di aur uske 6 parts bataye: plot, character, thought, diction, song, spectacle - plot sabse important, 'soul of tragedy'. Tragedy pity aur fear jagakar catharsis karti hai, jaise ro kar mann halka ho jaata hai. Hero mein ek galti hoti hai - hamartia. Peripeteia (ulti kismat) aur anagnorisis (pehchaan) best plot banate hain.
easy.trick: Tragedy ke 6 parts: 'PCT DSS' - Plot Character Thought, Diction Song Spectacle; catharsis = rone ke baad halka mann.

easy.title: Horace (65-8 BCE) and Longinus (1st century CE)
easy.story: Horace Roman poet the, unki Ars Poetica ek letter (Epistle to the Pisos) hai. Woh kehte hain poetry ko 'dulce et utile' hona chahiye - meethi bhi aur kaam ki bhi, jaise mithai mein dawai. Decorum, in medias res (kahani beech se shuru karo) aur 5 acts ka rule unhi ka hai. Longinus ne On the Sublime (Peri Hupsous) likha - badi soch, gehra josh wali writing jo humein 'transport' kar deti hai, sirf samjhati nahi. Unhone sublimity ke 5 sources bataye.
easy.trick: Horace = 'Halwa + Health' (delight and instruct); Longinus = 'Long-in-us' feeling jo andar tak le jaaye - sublime.

easy.title: Bharata and the Rasa Theory
easy.story: Bharata Muni ne Natyashastra likha, jise 'panchama veda' bhi kehte hain. Unka rasa sutra: vibhava, anubhava aur vyabhicari bhava ke sanyog se rasa ki nishpatti hoti hai. Jaise dal, masala, tadka mil kar swad banta hai, waise hi in sab se rasa banta hai. Bharata ne 8 rasa bataye, baad mein shanta ko 9th maana gaya. Har rasa ka ek sthayi bhava hota hai, jaise shringara ka rati, karuna ka shoka. Rasa sutra ke chaar famous commentators: Bhatta Lollata, Shankuka, Bhatta Nayaka, Abhinavagupta.
easy.trick: Rasa = khaana ka swaad; 'Vi-Anu-Vya' = Vibhava (cause), Anubhava (effect), Vyabhichari (passing mood); commentators 'Lo-Sha-Na-Abhi'.

easy.title: Dhvani: Anandavardhana and Abhinavagupta
easy.story: Anandavardhana ne Dhvanyaloka (9th century) mein kaha: 'kavyasyatma dhvanih' - kavya ki aatma dhvani (suggestion) hai. Jaise koi kahe 'suraj doob gaya' aur matlab ho 'ghar chalo', wahi chhupa arth dhvani hai. Word ki teen shaktiyan: abhidha (seedha arth), lakshana (indirect arth), vyanjana (suggested arth). Dhvani ke teen types: vastu, alankara aur rasa dhvani - rasa dhvani sabse ooncha. Abhinavagupta ne Dhvanyaloka par Locana aur Natyashastra par Abhinavabharati likhi.
easy.trick: Dhvani = 'ishaara samjho'; Ananda-'Dhvanyaloka', Abhinava-'Locana' (lochan = aankh jo dhvani ko dekhe).

easy.title: Alankara, Riti, Vakrokti and Auchitya Schools
easy.story: Alankara school (Bhamaha, Dandin): kavya ki sundarta gehno (alankara) se hai, jaise dulhan gehno se sajti hai. Riti school (Vamana, Kavyalankarasutravritti): 'ritir atma kavyasya' - style hi aatma hai; teen ritis - Vaidarbhi, Gaudi, Panchali. Vakrokti school (Kuntaka, Vakroktijivita): tedhi-meethi, alag tarah se kahi baat hi kavya hai. Auchitya school (Kshemendra, Auchityavicharacharcha): sab kuch 'uchit' yaani proper hona chahiye. Baad mein Mammata (Kavyaprakasha) aur Vishwanatha (Sahityadarpana: 'vakyam rasatmakam kavyam') ne sab ko jodha.
easy.trick: 'BhaDa - Va - Ku - Kshe': Bhamaha-Dandin Alankara, Vamana Riti, Kuntaka Vakrokti, Kshemendra Auchitya.

easy.title: Sir Philip Sidney: An Apology for Poetry
easy.story: Stephen Gosson ne The School of Abuse (1579) mein poetry ko gandi cheez kaha. Sidney ne jawab mein An Apology for Poetry (Defence of Poesie) likha, jo 1595 mein chhapa. Unhone kaha poet philosopher (sirf theory) aur historian (sirf facts) dono se upar hai, kyunki poet 'golden world' banata hai. Poetry 'teach and delight' karti hai. Woh English drama mein unities todne ki shikayat bhi karte hain.
easy.trick: Sidney = 'Sidhi Defence' - Gosson ka gussa, Sidney ka jawab; poet = sone ki duniya banane wala sunar.

easy.title: John Dryden: Father of English Criticism
easy.story: Dr Johnson ne Dryden ko 'father of English criticism' kaha. Unka An Essay of Dramatic Poesy (1668) ek dialogue hai jisme chaar log Thames par boat mein baat karte hain: Crites, Eugenius, Lisideius aur Neander. Neander (Dryden khud) English drama aur Shakespeare ka paksh leta hai. Dryden ne Shakespeare ko 'the largest and most comprehensive soul' kaha aur Chaucer ke liye 'here is God's plenty'. Unhone rhyme in drama ka bhi defence kiya.
easy.trick: Boat ke 4 yatri 'CELN' - Crites (Ancients), Eugenius (Moderns), Lisideius (French), Neander (English = Dryden).

easy.title: Alexander Pope and Samuel Johnson
easy.story: Pope ne An Essay on Criticism (1711) poem ki form mein likha - 'Follow Nature', 'A little learning is a dangerous thing', 'To err is human, to forgive divine'. Woh Neoclassical the, rules aur ancients ko maante the. Dr Johnson ne Preface to Shakespeare (1765) mein Shakespeare ko 'poet of nature' kaha aur unities of time-place ko bekaar bataya. Lives of the English Poets (1779-81) mein Metaphysical poets ke liye kaha 'heterogeneous ideas yoked by violence together'. Rasselas mein 'streaks of the tulip' wali line bhi unki hai.
easy.trick: Pope = poem mein criticism; Johnson = Dictionary wala dada jo Shakespeare ko 'nature ka poet' bole.

easy.title: William Wordsworth and S. T. Coleridge
easy.story: Wordsworth ne Lyrical Ballads ke Preface (1800, badha hua 1802) mein kaha poetry 'spontaneous overflow of powerful feelings' hai jo 'emotion recollected in tranquillity' se aati hai. Unhone aam logon ki bhasha ('language really used by men') ki baat ki. Coleridge ne Biographia Literaria (1817) mein imagination (primary, secondary) aur fancy ka fark samjhaya. Imagination naya banati hai, fancy sirf jodti hai - jaise chef vs sandwich jodne wala. 'Willing suspension of disbelief' bhi unka hai.
easy.trick: Words-worth = feelings ka overflow; Cole-ridge = Imagination ki 'ridge' (oonchai), fancy neeche.

easy.title: P. B. Shelley, Matthew Arnold and Walter Pater
easy.story: Shelley ki A Defence of Poetry (1821 mein likhi, 1840 mein chhapi) Peacock ke The Four Ages of Poetry ka jawab thi; famous line: 'Poets are the unacknowledged legislators of the world'. Arnold ne poetry ko 'criticism of life' kaha aur 'touchstone method' diya - mahaan kaviyon ki lines se nayi poetry ko jaancho. The Function of Criticism at the Present Time mein 'disinterestedness' aur 'the best that is known and thought' ki baat ki. Pater ne The Renaissance (1873) ke Conclusion mein kaha 'burn always with this hard, gem-like flame' - art for art's sake.
easy.trick: Shelley = 'unacknowledged MLA' (legislator); Arnold = touchstone (sona parakhne ka pathar); Pater = gem-like flame.

easy.title: T. S. Eliot as Critic
easy.story: Eliot ne Tradition and the Individual Talent (1919) mein kaha poet ko 'historical sense' chahiye aur poetry 'escape from emotion' hai, emotion ka bahaav nahi - impersonality. Unhone poet ke mind ko catalyst (platinum ka tukda) jaisa kaha. Hamlet and His Problems (1919) mein 'objective correlative' diya - emotion dikhane ke liye objects, situation, events ka set. The Metaphysical Poets (1921) mein 'dissociation of sensibility' - 17th century ke baad soch aur feeling alag ho gaye. Ye essays The Sacred Wood (1920) aur Selected Essays mein hain.
easy.trick: Eliot ka 'TOD': Tradition (1919), Objective correlative (Hamlet 1919), Dissociation (Metaphysical Poets 1921); platinum = catalyst.

easy.title: I. A. Richards and William Empson
easy.story: I. A. Richards ne Cambridge mein students ko bina naam ke poems diye aur unke jawab par Practical Criticism (1929) likhi. Principles of Literary Criticism (1924) mein emotive vs referential language aur poetry ko 'pseudo-statement' kaha. Meaning ke chaar kind: sense, feeling, tone, intention. The Philosophy of Rhetoric mein metaphor ke tenor aur vehicle diye. Unke student William Empson ne Seven Types of Ambiguity (1930) likhi - ek line ke kai matlab hona poetry ki taakat hai.
easy.trick: Richards = 'STFI' (Sense Tone Feeling Intention) + Tenor-Vehicle; Empson = 7 ka chakkar (Seven Types).

easy.title: F. R. Leavis
easy.story: F. R. Leavis Cambridge ke critic the aur Scrutiny (1932-53) magazine chalate the. The Great Tradition (1948) mein kaha English novel ki mahaan parampara Jane Austen, George Eliot, Henry James aur Joseph Conrad hai (baad mein D. H. Lawrence bhi). New Bearings in English Poetry (1932) aur Revaluation (1936) bhi unki hain. Woh literature ko moral seriousness aur 'life' se jodte the. C. P. Snow ke 'Two Cultures' par unka bada jhagda famous hai.
easy.trick: Leavis ki 'Great Tradition' team: 'A-GE-HJ-C' - Austen, George Eliot, Henry James, Conrad; Scrutiny = unka akhbaar.

easy.title: New Criticism: Ransom, Brooks, Tate, Wimsatt and Beardsley
easy.story: New Critics kehte the - poem ko 'close reading' se padho, poet ki life ya reader ka feeling mat dekho. Naam John Crowe Ransom ki book The New Criticism (1941) se aaya. Cleanth Brooks ne The Well Wrought Urn (1947) mein paradox, irony aur 'heresy of paraphrase' samjhaye. Wimsatt aur Beardsley ne 'intentional fallacy' aur 'affective fallacy' diye - The Verbal Icon (1954). Allen Tate ne 'tension' term diya. Brooks aur Warren ki Understanding Poetry (1938) college textbook bani.
easy.trick: Poem = bandh dabba (urn); andar dekho, bahar nahi - 'IA fallacy': Intentional (poet ki niyat) aur Affective (reader ka asar) dono mana.

easy.title: Northrop Frye: Archetypal Criticism
easy.story: Canadian critic Northrop Frye ne Anatomy of Criticism (1957) likhi. Unhone kaha poori literature ek system hai jisme baar baar aane wale patterns - archetypes - hain. Chaar mythoi seasons se jude hain: comedy = spring, romance = summer, tragedy = autumn, irony/satire = winter. Book mein chaar essays hain: historical (modes), ethical (symbols), archetypal (myths), rhetorical (genres). Jaise har saal mausam ghoomte hain, waise kahaniyan bhi ghoomti hain.
easy.trick: Frye ka mausam: 'Spring-Comedy (Holi ka mazaa), Summer-Romance, Autumn-Tragedy (patte girna), Winter-Irony'.

easy.title: Russian Formalism
easy.story: Russian Formalists (1910s-20s) kehte the literature ko 'kaise likha' se samjho, 'kya likha' se nahi. Viktor Shklovsky ne 'Art as Technique' (1917) mein 'ostranenie' yaani defamiliarization diya - jaani-pehchani cheez ko ajnabi bana kar dikhana, taaki 'make the stone stony'. Roman Jakobson ne 'literariness' ko study ka asli object kaha. Fabula (ghatnaon ka asli kram) aur syuzhet (kahani mein dikhaya gaya kram) ka fark bhi inka hai. Groups: OPOYAZ (St Petersburg) aur Moscow Linguistic Circle; Vladimir Propp ne folktale ke 31 functions diye.
easy.trick: Shklovsky = 'Shock-lovsky' - roz ki cheez ko shock bana do (defamiliarize); fabula = asli film, syuzhet = editing wala version.

quotes.quote: Tragedy, then, is an imitation of an action that is serious, complete, and of a certain magnitude ... through pity and fear effecting the proper purgation of these emotions.
Plot is the first principle and, as it were, the soul of a tragedy.
Poetry is more philosophical and of higher import than history.
Art is twice removed from truth (the imitation of an imitation).
Omne tulit punctum qui miscuit utile dulci (He has won every vote who has blended the useful with the sweet).
Sublimity is the echo of a great soul.
Vibhavanubhavavyabhicharisamyogad rasanishpattih (Rasa arises from the union of vibhava, anubhava and vyabhicharibhava).
Kavyasyatma dhvanih (Dhvani is the soul of poetry).
Ritir atma kavyasya (Riti is the soul of poetry).
Vakyam rasatmakam kavyam (Poetry is a sentence whose soul is rasa).
Vakroktih kavyajivitam (Vakrokti is the life of poetry).
Nature never set forth the earth in so rich tapestry as divers poets have done ... Her world is brazen, the poets only deliver a golden.
Now for the poet, he nothing affirms, and therefore never lieth.
He was the man who of all modern, and perhaps ancient poets, had the largest and most comprehensive soul.
A just and lively image of human nature.
quotes.by: John Dryden (Lisideius's definition of a play)

quotes.quote: Here is God's plenty.
quotes.source: Preface to Fables Ancient and Modern (1700)

quotes.quote: A little learning is a dangerous thing; / Drink deep, or taste not the Pierian spring.
True wit is Nature to advantage dressed, / What oft was thought, but ne'er so well expressed.
To err is human, to forgive divine.
For fools rush in where angels fear to tread.
Shakespeare is above all writers, at least above all modern writers, the poet of nature.
The most heterogeneous ideas are yoked by violence together.
quotes.source: Life of Cowley, Lives of the English Poets (1779-81)

quotes.quote: The business of a poet is to examine, not the individual, but the species ... he does not number the streaks of the tulip.
Poetry is the spontaneous overflow of powerful feelings: it takes its origin from emotion recollected in tranquillity.
Poetry is the breath and finer spirit of all knowledge.
A man speaking to men.
That willing suspension of disbelief for the moment, which constitutes poetic faith.
The primary Imagination I hold to be the living power and prime agent of all human perception.
Prose = words in their best order; poetry = the best words in the best order.
Negative capability, that is, when a man is capable of being in uncertainties, mysteries, doubts, without any irritable reaching after fact and reason.
Poets are the unacknowledged legislators of the world.
Poetry is at bottom a criticism of life.
quotes.source: Wordsworth (1879); developed in The Study of Poetry (1880)

quotes.quote: A disinterested endeavour to learn and propagate the best that is known and thought in the world.
quotes.source: The Function of Criticism at the Present Time (1864)

quotes.quote: To burn always with this hard, gem-like flame, to maintain this ecstasy, is success in life.
All art constantly aspires towards the condition of music.
quotes.source: The School of Giorgione, The Renaissance

quotes.quote: Poetry is not a turning loose of emotion, but an escape from emotion; it is not the expression of personality, but an escape from personality.
The progress of an artist is a continual self-sacrifice, a continual extinction of personality.
The only way of expressing emotion in the form of art is by finding an 'objective correlative'.
In the seventeenth century a dissociation of sensibility set in, from which we have never recovered.
Romanticism, then, ... is spilt religion.
Poetry is a pseudo-statement.
Literature is news that stays news.
The great English novelists are Jane Austen, George Eliot, Henry James and Joseph Conrad.
The language of poetry is the language of paradox.
The design or intention of the author is neither available nor desirable as a standard for judging the success of a work of literary art.
quotes.by: W. K. Wimsatt and Monroe C. Beardsley

quotes.quote: Art exists that one may recover the sensation of life; it exists to make one feel things, to make the stone stony.
The object of the science of literature is not literature but literariness.
A poem should not mean / But be.
